title: Finite presentation is closed under kernels, images, and cokernels over a coherent ring
statement: Let R be a commutative ring such that every finitely generated ideal of R is finitely presented. If f:M\to N is an R-linear map between finitely presented R-modules [def-sc-finitely-presented-module], then \operatorname{Ker}(f), \operatorname{Im}(f), and \operatorname{Coker}(f) are finitely presented R-modules [def-sc-finitely-presented-module].

source.place: Algebra, Lemma 05CW (coherent modules form an abelian category), together with Lemma 05CX (over a coherent ring, coherent modules are exactly finitely presented modules)

proof.text: Prove closure under finite products of the property that every finitely generated submodule is finitely presented (private Lean helper fp_submodule_prod). For a finitely generated S contained in A x B, the first projection has finitely generated image, hence finitely presented image by the property of A. Mathlib Module.FinitePresentation.fg_ker makes the kernel of S -> image finitely generated. The second projection embeds that kernel into B. Its image is finitely generated and thus finitely presented by the property of B; transport back along LinearEquiv.ofInjective. Mathlib Module.finitePresentation_of_ker now makes S finitely presented. Transport the submodule property along linear equivalences (fp_submodule_equiv).

source.place: Algebra, Definition 05CU and Lemmas 05CW, 05CX; implemented using Mathlib.Algebra.Module.FinitePresentation

proof.text: Induct on n to prove that every finitely generated submodule of R^n is finitely presented (fp_submodule_fin). For n=0 the submodule is subsingleton. For n+1 use the linear equivalence R^(n+1) = R x R^n and product closure from step 1. The property for R is exactly hR, since Ideal R is Submodule R R.

source.place: Algebra, Definition 05CU and Lemmas 05CW, 05CX; implemented using Mathlib.Algebra.Module.FinitePresentation

proof.text: Extend the property to every finitely presented module M (fp_fg_submodule). Take a surjection p:R^n -> M using Module.Finite.exists_fin'; its kernel is finitely generated by Module.FinitePresentation.fg_ker. For a finitely generated submodule S of M, its inverse image T has image S under p and contains ker p. Submodule.fg_of_fg_map_of_fg_inf_ker makes T finitely generated. Step 2 makes T finitely presented. The restricted map q:T -> S is surjective; ker q maps injectively to ker p under the subtype map, and its image equals ker p. Hence ker q is finitely generated by Submodule.fg_map_iff. Apply Module.finitePresentation_of_surjective to q to obtain finite presentation of S.

source.place: Algebra, Definition 05CU and Lemmas 05CW, 05CX; implemented using Mathlib.Algebra.Module.FinitePresentation

proof.text: The range of f is finitely generated by Submodule.fg_range; step 3 in N makes it finitely presented. Apply Module.FinitePresentation.fg_ker to the surjective range restriction M -> range f to make ker f finitely generated; step 3 in M makes it finitely presented. Finally the quotient map N -> N/range f is surjective with finitely generated kernel range f, so Module.finitePresentation_of_surjective gives the cokernel. Assemble the three conclusions.
